Among correct candidates, a lower abstract cost (the number of SSA instructions executed over all vectors) scores higher, and any correct candidate scores above any incorrect one. responses:
## Diagnosis

Every prior attempt left the cost at exactly 3549. Rearranging the tail ladder and hoisting `n` changed nothing measurable, so those edits were absorbed by the SSA optimizer. The cost is dominated by the main 16-word block, which runs for most of the work on longer vectors.

In that block, each `xs[k]` is a separate index expression. Even when the prove pass removes the bounds checks, the compiler still has to reason about each access. A single reslice `b := xs[:16]` gives one length check and constant indices into a fixed-length slice. This is the one change still left in the hot path.

The change keeps the same semantics: the function still returns the same value, still doesn't modify `xs`, and keeps the recursive peel for the tail. The `l == 16` early return and the tail ladder are untouched.
